bounded_observations: ACL 26-43 authorizes use of administrative data to establish specified exemptions, introduces the CDSS Exemption File, distinguishes automated, system, and worker updates, and requires ordinary worker review and documentation.

bounded_observations: ACL 26-29 issues the CalFresh ABAWD Time Limit Handbook Version 3.0 effective June 1, 2026.
The handbook permits self-attestation unless questionable, documentary evidence, collateral contacts, case-record evidence, and bounded county or eligibility-worker judgment.
The handbook establishes a county discretionary-exemption allocation, application, notice, and STAT 47 tracking framework.
limitations: The policy text does not prove uniform implementation or actual discretionary-exemption use.

field_decisions.finding_summary: California’s captured operative work-requirement and ABAWD authority is the CalFresh ABAWD Time Limit Handbook Version 3.0 issued through ACL 26-29, effective June 1, 2026, with ACL 26-43 as current supplemental administrative-data guidance.

observed_components.primary_instrument: ACL 26-29 / CalFresh ABAWD Time Limit Handbook Version 3.0

field_decisions.finding_summary: California’s allocation, county-use framework, notices, and STAT 47 tracking obligation are observed, but the fixed public corpus does not recover current actual discretionary-exemption use.

California’s captured guidance permits self-attestation unless questionable, documentary evidence, collateral contacts, case-record and administrative-data evidence, and bounded county or eligibility-worker judgment with documentation duties.
The current South Dakota manual is marked Updated July 2026, but the fixed corpus does not recover an exact effective date for the complete current implementation authority.
South Dakota’s FY2025 waiver is preserved as an expired predecessor, while the fixed corpus does not recover a complete current waiver approval and governing period.
The FY2026 plan anticipates 100 discretionary exemptions, but the fixed corpus does not recover observed South Dakota discretionary-exemption use or a complete state practice ledger.

Washington’s captured operative ABAWD authority is the permanent adoption WSR 26-10-028 for WAC 388-444-0030 and 388-444-0035, effective July 1, 2026, together with the current EA-Z ABAWD chapter and revision custody.

Washington’s captured current pages say all areas became subject to the time limit and no areas were waived as of February 1, 2026, but the complete current governing period or successor end state is not publicly recovered.

Washington’s current manual states the state’s discretionary-exemption authority and intended use categories, and the FY2026 plan anticipates 240 exemptions, but actual reported use is not publicly recovered.
